flags: Review each changed hunk before drafting findings. For each altered decision, trace a concrete input through the old and new behavior. Check boundary values, failure paths, and the contracts imposed by surrounding callers and tests. Verify suspected failures against the actual types, guards, and versions shown. Drop claims that the code contradicts, observations of correct behavior, and guesses that lack a failing scenario. Group repeated instances of one root cause into a single actionable finding, citing one changed line and mentioning other affected sites in its body.

findings.body: The new method isAccessTokenId in testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java has a logic error in the matchesSafely method. It splits the token ID string by ':', expects two parts, then checks if the substring of the first part from index 3 to 5 equals the expected grant shortcut. However, the condition incorrectly returns false if they are equal, which means it rejects valid token IDs with the expected grant shortcut. This will cause tests that rely on this matcher to fail incorrectly. The condition should be inverted to return false if they are not equal, and true if they are equal and the second part matches UUID format.
findings.suggestion: Change the condition in matchesSafely from `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` to `if (!items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.
findings.title: Incorrect logic in isAccessTokenId matcher causes false negatives in tests

models.summary: The change adds grant type shortcuts and encodes grant type info into token IDs, improving token identification and testing. However, there is a critical bug in the test matcher isAccessTokenId that will cause false negatives in tests verifying token IDs. Fixing this logic is necessary to avoid test failures.
